claims: Simultaneous next-to-leading order (NLO) Holstein-Primakoff expansion for both rotor I and quasiparticle j is necessary to preserve D2 Bohr symmetry and reproduce exact diagonalization at the symmetric limit.

Bohr & Mottelson Vol. 2 Eq. (4-282) and Figure 4-33 contains a typographical ordering inversion in the definition of asymmetry parameter kappa; the correct ordering is A1 >= A2 >= A3 (J1 <= J2 <= J3).

Hydrodynamic moments of inertia cannot be properly mapped onto BM-II Figure 4-33 as a function of kappa because J_z^hyd vanishes in the prolate limit gamma -> 0, unlike rigid MOI which maintains non-zero values on all three axes.

Rigid moments of inertia successfully reproduce the experimental observation that B(E2)out/B(E2)in is significantly enhanced for I - j = odd (wobbling bandhead) over I - j = even in 135Pr and 163Lu, whereas hydrodynamic MOI yields nearly identical values.

Hydrodynamic moments of inertia predict unphysically large B(M1)out/B(E2)in for I - j = even transitions that exceed those of I - j = odd, directly contradicting experimental non-observation of M1 out-of-band decay from even I - j states.

Microscopic Coriolis anti-pairing (CAP) from CONHFB provides analytical spin-dependent moments of inertia that reproduce the backbending in 135Pr (Fermi-type) and TSD multi-wobbling bands in 163Lu (rational fraction).
